text: The published @diegopetrucci/pi-claude-fast and @diegopetrucci/pi-openai-fast packages stay in the repo so those npm names keep resolving. Their bodies are deprecation notices: they do not read config, register commands, or inject Fast fields into requests. On startup they clear their leftover footer status and strip fast-mode-2026-02-01 from the current model header, because /reload keeps that state from the previous extension runtime. The collection continues to load only extensions/fast.
author: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

text: The repository owner explicitly approved dropping PowerShell tool support: remove the permission-gate analyzer and dedicated PowerShell CI coverage, and reject named powershell tool calls as unsupported rather than allowing unchecked execution. Keep Bash safety, other Windows compatibility, and clipboard/notification helpers that internally invoke PowerShell. Preserve historical release documentation. This support-scope decision does not drop Windows generally.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The standalone openai-fast and claude-fast extensions are retired. Future Fast mode work should target only the unified extensions/fast implementation; do not extend the retired standalone variants.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Fable 5.2 Fast (Nov 2026, PR #217, approved by Diego): kept the single global /fast toggle instead of copying Claude Code's per-model opt-in (where Fast only re-enables on Fable 5.2 if turned on while on Fable). The $16/$80 auto-apply risk is documented in the fast README Notes instead. Opus 4.8 was removed from the Anthropic allowlist (PR #218) before Anthropic's 2026-11-30 cutoff by Diego's choice, not waiting for the API to start rejecting it.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The README downloads badge is a shields.io endpoint badge that reads npm-downloads.json from the orphan 'badges' branch. The scheduled download-badge workflow regenerates that file with scripts/npm-download-total.mjs. The user wants the badge to show all-time downloads summed across every package in the repo, not just the root package. Two alternatives were rejected. shields.io npm/dt counts a single package only. Also, the npm downloads API silently clamps any range to the last 18 months without returning an error (observed 2026-11-10: a 1000-01-01:3000-01-01 query came back starting 2025-05-11), so npm/dt stops being all-time after 18 months. The JSON goes on a separate branch because main has a PR-required repository ruleset that a bot push cannot satisfy, and daily bot commits would clutter main history.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: For a future agent-workflow-audit extension, the user wants the distilled final audit results returned to the main session. The isolation goal is to keep intermediate discovery, command runs, raw errors, retries, and tool transcript out of the main session context, not to hide the final report.

Fast allowlists stay hardcoded (Diego, Nov 2026). The Fast allowlists were brought up to date with the vendors' current docs. Codex and direct-API GPT-6.1 Terra were added, which supersedes tvdxhy's Terra hold. Considered and rejected: (a) dropping the allowlists entirely. Anthropic rejects speed=fast on unsupported models, and Fast follows model switches, so a config default of enabled:true would break Sonnet/Haiku requests. Pi also shows Fast status and 2x cost even when the tier is ignored. (b) Deriving Codex eligibility from the service_tiers field of chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models, which is what the Codex CLI does. Rejected as an authenticated network call plus caching and failure handling that only helps Codex. (c) A user config setting for extra models. Rejected because a wrong entry fails the same way as having no allowlist. When OpenAI or Anthropic ship a new model, update the lists by hand from the vendor docs. For Codex, openai/codex codex-rs/models-manager/models.json is a good source.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The user chose canonical source with checked-in generated copies for sharing code between independently installable extensions, after considering parity-only duplication, shared npm dependencies, and build/pack-time generation. The approved first slice is the Glimpse wrapper and its declarations for the two annotation extensions; footers and subagent helpers remain follow-up work.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The gnosis pi extension is intentionally agent-facing only: it exposes a gnosis tool but does not add user slash commands because the user explicitly said commands were unnecessary. Keep future UX changes aligned with that unless requested.

Pi 1.5.0 catalog ranking (decided by Diego, Nov 2026): GPT-6.1 Terra ranks below every Sol tier and above GPT-5.6 Terra (tier-before-version: Sol > Terra > Luna), matched by exact ID so :batch/-fast aliases are not picked; on OpenRouter -pro ranks above the base. Kimi K3.1 Pro ranks above K3, with K3.1 Pro HighSpeed between them. Terra is NOT added to the fast-mode allowlist until OpenAI fast/priority-tier support is verified. Librarian's cost-led switch on kimi-coding from k3-256k to kimi-for-coding (caused by K3-256K's new 3/15 pricing) was accepted as-is.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: quiet-tools on Pi <1.0.1 (no registerToolRenderer): Diego chose to show a one-time notice and leave rendering untouched rather than keep the old approach of re-registering the 7 built-in tools as a fallback. Re-registration was dropped entirely in the Pi 1.0.4 update.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Decision history for project-mcp-json: initially a Claude-style per-file approval (path+sha256) was built because Pi auto-trusts dirs with no Pi-recognized protected resources, so a root-only .mcp.json would otherwise run with no prompt. User then rejected the separate approval: 'if the dir is approved already the mcps should be too', and wants alignment with Pi's own trust semantics (incl. parent-dir trust inheritance). Current design: treat root .mcp.json like a Pi trust-requiring resource — require isProjectTrusted; accept Pi's real decision when protected resources exist; else nearest-ancestor saved trust.json decision; else defaultProjectTrust (ask => skip + suggest /trust). The extension never writes trust.json. Out of scope: Codex .codex/config.toml import, parent-dir .mcp.json discovery.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Pi 1.5.0 ladder gap refresh (approved by Diego, Nov 2026): Opus 5.5 deliberately stays above Fable 5.1 on Anthropic-compatible ladders (Fable costs 2.5x). Mistral Large 4 ranks above Medium 3.5 despite Mistral listing it as Public Preview. Gemini 4 Argon replaces Gemini 3.1 Pro as the top Gemini entry but keeps Gemini's slot behind Claude/GPT on mixed providers, because Google's own model card puts it behind GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5 on FrontierSWE/Terminal-bench; its $2/$10 price is introductory until 2026-11-30 (then $4/$20). OpenCode Go keeps DeepSeek V4 Pro above Kimi K3.1 Pro only because no benchmark evidence could be verified; revisit if evidence appears. code-reviewer now covers every provider by copying oracle ladders for providers it lacked, but its pre-existing per-provider ladders intentionally keep their GPT-first / Bedrock Sonnet-5-over-GPT-6.1-Sol policy and are NOT parity-locked to oracle.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Old Pi versions are not a concern (Diego, Oct 2026, PR #186 review). Fast now adds fast-mode-2026-02-01 via the request payload 'betas' list, which only works on Pi >=0.85.0; on Pi 0.84.x (including the 0.84.4 .pi-fleet-tested-version marker) Anthropic Fast would send 'betas' in the JSON body without the beta header. Diego explicitly chose not to add a VERSION gate or a minimum-version note for this.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The unified Fast extension should be added without deleting or replacing the existing openai-fast and claude-fast standalone packages. The root @diegopetrucci/pi-extensions bundle should auto-load only the unified extension; the two provider-specific Fast extensions remain available as standalone packages but become standalone-only.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Subagent MCP policy (decided by Diego, Pi 1.0.4 update, Oct 2026): all six subagent extensions (oracle, contrarian, code-reviewer, librarian, triage-comments, agent-workflow-audit) get ALL configured MCP tools via mcp__* + tool_search + the 3 resource tools. Explicitly chosen over filtering to readOnlyHint tools, and codemode was deliberately NOT exposed. Side-effect risk is handled by prompt guidance (evidence-only) rather than tool filtering. For SDK-session subagents Diego chose to actually load the MCP/tool_search built-ins (option A) over limiting MCP to the CLI-spawned oracle/contrarian; MCP loads only on host Pi >=1.0.4 and a project mcp.json only when the host trusts the project and the subagent shares its cwd. Rejected: passing --no-mcp or any new CLI flag to child pi, because Pi 1.0.0-1.0.3 parse unknown --flags as consuming the next argument.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: When copying/adapting upstream pi example extensions into this repo, include README attribution with a link back to the original upstream example, following the existing notify README pattern.

npm 11.17.0 can produce byte-different gzip wrappers for the same package when run under Node 24.11.1 versus Node 26.5.0, even though the gunzipped tar payload bytes are identical. This surfaced while manually bootstrapping @diegopetrucci/pi-fast@0.1.0 before the Node 24-pinned OIDC workflow. Release verification must compare exact tar payloads as a bounded fallback rather than assuming gzip-level hash reproducibility across Node runtimes.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>
